study_context: continental Sandhills prairie insect-reduction life-cycle experiment

study_context: California coastal dunes old vs new dune
demographic_gate: seed-limited recruitment in both dune contexts
quantitative_anchor: new dune seed RR=877/360=2.44 and seedling RR=6.0/2.2=2.73; old dune seed RR=1954/470=4.16 and seedling RR=3.3/1.28=2.58
claim_boundary: Habitat contrasts are descriptive transmission tests rather than a pooled environmental moderator coefficient

study_context: Nebraska tallgrass prairie five sites × low/high productivity zones
demographic_gate: density dependence tested but not detected
quantitative_anchor: Δlambda>0 at every site×zone, range 0.3–1.2; productivity×treatment F1,16=0.05 P=0.82; fecundity was the main demographic pathway
claim_boundary: IPM outputs are model-derived demographic effects and are not pooled with raw seed lnRR

quantitative_anchor: herbivore exclusion allowed low-density lambda>5 whereas herbivore access drove lambda<1; qualitative suppression persisted across sites and density dependence muted effects mainly at high density
claim_boundary: Hierarchical demographic model; exact site-level effect sizes are not treated as independent studies

study_context: Kansas restored tallgrass prairie seven-year fertilizer × herbivore-exclusion experiment with prescribed fire
quantitative_anchor: insects reduced seed production (F1,62=6.45 P=0.014); population growth effect occurred in 2/3 fire transitions vs 1/4 non-fire transitions; fertilization moderated herbivore effects in only 1/7 transitions
claim_boundary: Independent from DTR03; fire inference is a repeated-transition pattern rather than a randomized fire treatment

study_context: Colorado peripheral montane populations across five sites and 52% of regional elevation range
quantitative_anchor: floral herbivory reduced lifetime viable seed production at all sites but extra seed did not produce proportional recruitment; elevation changed phenology but not damage seed production or recruitment
claim_boundary: Seed effect overlaps the current seed-output meta dataset but the recruitment result is a separate downstream estimand
